there is a consistent relationship between positive attitudes to ICT and desirable approaches to studying, and that this relationship is not affected by the age of the students, or by whether they are studying face-to-face, or at a distance.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
students who have positive attitudes to ICT and who are more confident in using them are more likely to engage with the material and to adopt more effective approaches to studying.
the use of ICT in higher education is a key component of the learning experience of students and is likely to become even more important in the near future.
the use of ICT has a positive influence on students’ learning, especially when it is integrated in a blended learning approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
students who have positive attitudes to ICT use are more likely to be self-directed learners and to adopt a more active approach to their studies.
students who adopt more positive attitudes to technology also tend to adopt more positive approaches to learning.
students who are positive about ICTs are more inclined to adopt approaches to studying that are desirable for their learning and for their personal and social development.
